definitions.explanation: In a way that makes little or no noise. Used as a command to tell someone to be quiet, or to describe actions done without making sound.
In a calm, undisturbed manner. Describes doing something without haste, excitement, or agitation.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんが{寝|ね}ているから、{静|しず}かに{歩|ある}いて。
examples.english: The baby is sleeping, so walk quietly.

examples.japanese: ドアを{静|しず}かに{閉|し}めた。
{彼|かれ}は{静|しず}かに{微笑|ほほえ}んだ。
{雪|ゆき}が{静|しず}かに{降|ふ}り{積|つ}もっていた。
examples.english: The snow was quietly piling up.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Adverbial form of the na-adjective {静|しず}か. Functions as an adverb modifying verbs. Also used as a command: {静|しず}かに！(Be quiet!)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {静|しず}かにする (to be quiet; to keep quiet)
- {静|しず}かに{暮|く}らす (to live peacefully)
- {静|しず}かに{話|はな}す (to speak softly)
- {静|しず}かに{待|ま}つ (to wait quietly)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- おとなしく: obediently, meekly — implies compliance
- そっと: softly, stealthily — emphasizes gentleness or secrecy
- ひっそり: in seclusion, inconspicuously — emphasizes being unnoticed
